assumptions: Fin count = the catalogue's 'Max # Fins' for the profile: the rating configuration is taken to be the fully populated base, which is the configuration the catalogue's own part-numbering example builds.

Fin height H is the height of the fins above the top face of the base extrusion (the order guide lists fin height as a dimension separate from the base extrusion profile, whose thickness is the table's T). Total assembly height = T + H.

The catalogue does not state which finish its thermal ratings were taken with; finish is recorded as not stated. The toy model has no radiation term in any case, so a finish-dependent radiation contribution, if any, sits inside the residual error and inside what the single fitted coefficient absorbs on the calibration subset.

The model derives fin spacing from plate width, fin count, and fin thickness (even spacing, edge to edge); the real gap implied by the catalogue pitch (FP - FT) differs slightly. The pitch is recorded per part for provenance.

Model comparison uses the unpenalised heat core (model.heat_watts): the demo scorer's spacing/mass penalties are search constructs for evolution, not physics, and have no counterpart in a datasheet rating.
catalogue_facts_used: Table columns: Extrusion Profile No. | Base W | Base T | FT (fin thickness) | FP (fin pitch) | Max # Fins | Thermal resistance degC/W, Natural Convection at fin height H = 2 in and H = 4 in | Forced Convection (not used here).

Note 1: natural and forced convection thermal resistances are based on 6.000 in. length for profiles less than 8.000 in. wide. All profiles selected here are < 8 in wide, so every configuration below is 6.000 in (152.4 mm) long.
Order guide (example BE8546-1200-U4W): profile, length in inches, finish, fin height in inches, mounting option. Fin height is an orderable dimension of the fins themselves.

Known source defect: for profile 8711 the catalogue's parenthetical metric fin pitch reads 5.4 mm, which contradicts its own inch value (0.275 in = 6.99 mm); the inch value is consistent with Max # Fins x FP ~= base width for every row (e.g. 10 x 0.275 = 2.75 ~= 2.800), so inch values are used throughout and the parenthetical for that one cell is treated as a misprint.
description: Real commercial bonded-fin heatsink configurations from Wakefield Engineering's bonded fin catalogue, used to calibrate the Hortus toy scorer (model.py). Every geometry and measured value below was read from the catalogue document itself on 2026-11-01; nothing is estimated except the explicitly listed assumptions.

primary_source.document: Custom Bonded Fin Heat Sinks and Assemblies catalogue, 'Bonded Fin Bases' table (p. 54)
primary_source.hosting_note: Manufacturer's catalogue document hosted on a third-party mirror; the document itself is Wakefield's (their contact block and order guide are in it).

property_sources.what: Alloy: aluminium 6063-T5, Wakefield's stated heatsink extrusion alloy ('THE Heat Sink Alloy - Aluminum 6063-T5', Wakefield Heat Sink Technologies document)
Thermal conductivity of aluminium 6063-T5: k = 209 W/m-K (ASM Material Data Sheet, 'AA; Typical at 77F')

shared_conditions.delta_t: not stated in the source for the bases table; the model's predicted thermal resistance is independent of delta_t (Q is linear in delta_t), so this does not block comparison
shared_conditions.length_basis: 6.000 in (152.4 mm), catalogue note 1 (profiles < 8 in wide)
